functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: Lies deep to (behind) pectineus and adductor longus, sandwiched between the anterior and posterior branches of the obturator nerve, which it is classically used to separate surgically.
functional_compartments.source: Ward SR, Eng CM, Smallwood LH, Lieber RL (2009) Clin Orthop Relat Res 467:1074-1082 -- lower-extremity muscle architecture (fascicle length, PCSA, sarcomere length) cadaver dataset

motor_endplate_zones.method: cadaveric dissection motor-point mapping, 19 limbs from 10 adult cadavers
motor_endplate_zones.notes: Motor point measured at 21.0% +/- 4.8% (mean +/- SD, expressed here as a range) along the pubic-tubercle-to-medial-epicondyle line. The same study also placed the motor point at 24.9% +/- 7.4% along a horizontal line from the pubic tubercle to the greater trochanter. A separate pediatric Sihler-staining study (Yan Y et al. 2019, Front Neurol 10:616, doi:10.3389/fneur.2019.00616) qualitatively found the densest terminal-nerve region 'at the center of the muscle belly, extending from the upper-medial region to the lower-lateral region,' consistent with a proximal-to-mid-belly target.
motor_endplate_zones.source: Kwon JY, Kim JS, Lee WI (2009) Am J Phys Med Rehabil 88(4):336-341, doi:10.1097/PHM.0b013e3181619435 -- retrieved via PubMed

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Ward SR, Eng CM, Smallwood LH, Lieber RL (2009) Clin Orthop Relat Res 467:1074-1082 -- lower-extremity muscle architecture (fascicle length, PCSA, sarcomere length) cadaver dataset
